extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsroom managers, and media scholars interested in race and local news coverage
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluate and reform local news programs' practices and newsworthiness decisions to identify why people of color are under-covered and how coverage could be made more representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incognizant racism
rubrics_metrics.description: News workers consistently ignore news in significant portions of communities they cover without being aware of doing so; not overt racism but systematic blind spots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies a new theoretical concept: coverage gaps are produced by everyday newsroom practices and perceptions rather than explicit hostile intent. Use this lens to look for unconscious omission patterns rather than only explicit discriminatory acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of events considered newsworthy (favoring white communities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suburb school board meetings; white-owned business openings; white churches' charity events; white teen sports teams; crime AGAINST white victims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These concrete examples show what routine 'news' looks like in practice: everyday civic, commercial, religious, and school life of white communities is routinely treated as newsworthy. Use such lists to audit what kinds of routine events are covered and whose routine life is made visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine community life visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Routine stories reflect the dominant group's life; everyday community life of communities of color is often invisible in local coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether 'routine' beats and daily coverage include community meetings, schools, churches, and social life across racial groups rather than only those of the dominant group. An anti-pattern is equating 'routine' with the majority's routine while ignoring other groups' routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exoticization of cultural events
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultural events in communities of color are labeled 'ethnic' and presented as exoticized features rather than routine community life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for framing that treats non-dominant cultures as spectacle or exception. Good practice: present cultural events as part of the ordinary civic life of communities rather than as 'other'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crime-focused, racialized coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Neighborhoods labeled 'high-crime' are covered primarily for crime; crime coverage is racialized, and crimes against white victims receive more attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether coverage of a neighborhood is dominated by crime stories and whether that pattern corresponds to reporter assumptions rather than balanced reporting. Anti-pattern: reducing an area to crime stories only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source rolodex composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Source rolodexes skew white, meaning reporters' contact lists favor white individuals and institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the diversity of sources used: who appears as experts, spokespeople, grassroots voices. Guidance: actively expand and diversify contact lists; measure how often sources from different racial groups appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat structures that avoid minority neighborhoods
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsroom beat assignments and structures systematically avoid minority neighborhoods, reducing routine coverage of those communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine beat maps and assignment patterns to see which neighborhoods receive routine reporting. Reform: reconfigure beats or assignments to ensure equitable geographic and community coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporters' residential and social proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters frequently do not live in the communities of color they cover, contributing to lack of relationships and awareness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider reporters' lived experience and proximity to communities as a factor in coverage equity. Good practice: recruit and retain reporters with local ties; encourage community immersion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial agenda set by majority-white editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial decisions are made by mostly white managers, which shapes what is considered newsworthy and sets the news agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate decision-making hierarchies and who controls story selection. Recommendation: diversify editorial leadership and incorporate community input in agenda-setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'White news' phenomenon (appearance of inclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'White news' delivered by non-white anchors creates the appearance of inclusion even when substantive coverage of communities of color is lacking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between surface diversity (on-air faces) and substantive representational practices (whose stories are told). Avoid treating visible minorities on-air as evidence that coverage is equitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on press releases from elite (white) institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases from elite, often white, institutions are privileged as news leads, skewing coverage toward those institutions' activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit sources of story leads. Anti-pattern: uncritical reliance on institutional press releases that reproduces elite-centric news agendas. Good practice: seek story leads originating within diverse communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to consult Spanish-language and alternative media
rubrics_metrics.description: Spanish-language media and other community media are not consulted, reducing awareness and coverage of issues important to non-English-speaking communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include outreach to ethnic and language-specific media as a routine reporting practice. Use these outlets to identify sources, events, and perspectives otherwise missed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Under-coverage of Indigenous nations
rubrics_metrics.description: Indigenous nations and issues are particularly under-covered within local news ecosystems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure coverage frequency and depth for Indigenous communities separately; build relationships with tribal reporters, leaders, and institutions to improve representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of source relationships as exclusion factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Communities of color are excluded when reporters lack source relationships in those communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether reporters have established, trusted relationships across communities. Remedy: intentional relationship-building and long-term beats focused on trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations: diversify newsroom staff at all levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Diversify newsroom staff at all levels (not just on-air) to change hiring, sourcing, and editorial decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an actionable reform: hire and promote journalists of color into reporting and managerial roles; evaluate hiring and promotion practices for bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations: diversify sources and contact lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively diversify sources/contact lists so that reporting draws on a broader, representative set of voices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set measurable targets for source diversity, track source demographics, and create processes for regularly updating contact lists to include community organizations, faith leaders, businesses, and residents of color.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations: cover positive community life of all communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Intentionally cover positive, routine community life across racial and ethnic groups rather than only crime or 'exotic' events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial planning should include beats or story quotas that surface everyday civic life (schools, local businesses, charities, sports) in under-covered communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations: editorial accountability and representation audits
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement editorial accountability for representation, including audits of who appears in stories and how communities are framed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use regular audits to measure representation (who appears, which neighborhoods are covered, story framings). Accountability mechanisms can include published diversity metrics, editorial reviews, and corrective plans.
